questions.q: What does this lesson's framework add on top of Data Governance Foundations Lesson 12's five organizational questions?
options: Five architectural factors that determine which reference-architecture pattern can actually be built
An entirely unrelated set of questions about office furniture budgets
Nothing — it simply repeats Foundations Lesson 12 verbatim
A requirement to always choose data mesh regardless of circumstances
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly builds on, rather than repeats, Foundations Lesson 12, adding architectural factors about what can actually be built.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what happens if an organization adopts data mesh without funding a real self-serve platform?
options: It produces decentralization with mesh vocabulary, not actual federated computational governance
The governance model works identically regardless of platform investment
It automatically becomes a centralized hub-and-spoke architecture instead
Nothing changes — platform investment is irrelevant to governance
questions.explain: The lesson warns that mesh without funded platform investment just becomes decentralization using mesh terminology.

questions.q: According to the five factors, what should an organization with strong metadata management but weak lineage tracking do?
options: Target the specific gap (lineage) rather than rebuilding the whole architecture
Discard its existing metadata management entirely and start over
Switch immediately to a fully decentralized model
Ignore the capability map entirely since it's never useful
questions.explain: The lesson's first factor states the specific capability gap, not the whole architecture, should usually drive the next investment.

questions.q: In the worked insurance-company example, which model do the five factors point toward?
options: A federated rollout scoped specifically to claims and underwriting, with marketing staying separately governed
A full, unscoped data-mesh rollout across all three domains immediately
A fully centralized model covering all three domains with one hub
No governance architecture at all, since insurance data doesn't need it
questions.explain: Given cross-cutting regulated data in claims/underwriting but independent marketing data, limited platform budget, and existing capability gaps, the factors point to a narrowly scoped federated model.

questions.q: What does this lesson say Chapter 3 covers next?
options: Metadata and catalog architecture, the capability this chapter leaned on without building it out in full
A full repeat of Chapter 2's operating models
Payroll and HR systems architecture
The course ends after this lesson
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly previews Chapter 3 as metadata and catalog architecture, building on what this chapter assumed throughout.
